commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions (#24966)

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves, and
add the function pass
`iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-data-tiling-encodings` for propagation
outside dispatches. Hoisting keeps its existing behavior. The new pass
stops at existing dispatches and block boundaries, and constant CSE
stays disabled because Flow regions do not materialize constants
themselves.

- `iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings` runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps `set_encoding` with `tensor.cast`
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
They stay separate until bubbling through generic ops goes through the
encoding propagation interfaces (TODO(#20179)).
- Bubbling now stops at `set_encoding` ops whose encoding is not an
`EncodingAttr`, such as `#iree_encoding.padding`, instead of crashing.
`iree-dispatch-creation-hoist-encoding-ops` could already hit this
within dispatches; both passes have a regression test.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental
early data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

commit_message:
[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan SPIR-V e2e tests under rocjitsu (#24990)

Add CPU-hosted Vulkan compute e2e coverage for gfx1100 and gfx1201 to
the existing Linux Clang CI job alongside the six ROCm targets. Move
that job to Ubuntu 24.04 with official Mesa RADV and Vulkan
validation-layer packages, and let RADV compile the existing SPIR-V
modules to each simulated GPU's instructions.

Keep one job, one regular IREE build, and one packaged TheRock SDK
pinned to `10.2.0a20261006`. Preserve `build_all.sh` and regular CTest
coverage, then reuse the build for HIP and Vulkan. The wheel's rocjitsu
revision `81d4fa340ce8` includes the SDMA count fix from
https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12708.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before CTest.
Use eight simulator test workers, a 60-minute Vulkan step timeout, and
per-target logs and JUnit results. Run both simulator suites after a
successful build even if an earlier test suite fails.

The fresh build also exposed a missing dependency on generated
`PluginABIHash.h`; explicitly order generation before its consumers
compile.

Assisted-by: codex

commit_message:
[CI] Run Vulkan HAL CTS under rocjitsu

Extend the Vulkan simulator helper to select HAL CTS alongside the
existing e2e tests on gfx1100 and gfx1201. Reuse the same CI job, build,
and pinned TheRock SDK.

Give the raw SPIR-V CTS executable a five-minute timeout. Its concurrent
replay case submits two dispatches of 8M workgroups and takes just over
a minute on simulated gfx1100, exceeding the previous 60-second limit.
Regenerate the CMake test definition from Bazel.

The assertions-enabled local run passes all 192 selected test executables
on each GPU, including 43 HAL CTS executables, with existing per-case
capability skips retained. Shell, actionlint, and pre-commit checks pass.

Assisted-by: codex

[CI] Run Vulkan HAL CTS under rocjitsu

Extend the Vulkan simulator helper to select HAL CTS alongside the
existing e2e tests on gfx1100 and gfx1201. Reuse the same CI job, build,
and pinned TheRock SDK.

Give the raw SPIR-V CTS executable a five-minute timeout. Its concurrent
replay case submits two dispatches of 8M workgroups and takes just over
a minute on simulated gfx1100, exceeding the previous 60-second limit.
Regenerate the CMake test definition from Bazel.

The assertions-enabled local run passes all 192 selected test executables
on each GPU, including 43 HAL CTS executables, with existing per-case
capability skips retained. Shell, actionlint, and pre-commit checks pass.

Assisted-by: codex

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-channel-group quantization to LinalgExt

Convert the typed PT2E quantize_per_channel_group and
dequantize_per_channel_group ops to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and
dequantize_affine before Torch-to-Linalg expands them, so later QDQ
optimizations keep the group structure instead of floordiv-indexed
arithmetic. LinalgExt indexes parameters with projected permutations, so
the ops work on the input with its last dimension split into groups and
their result is collapsed back; the type of that view is derived from
the group size in one place. A group size beyond the row with one scale
per row is read as a single group spanning the row, as PT2E does.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express remain for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering:
groups that do not evenly split a static last dimension of a rank-2
input, flattened group parameters, bool zero points, which LinalgExt
would sign-extend to -1, non-float real values, and f16 or bf16 scales
on quantize, which would round f32 real values and currently fail to
link on llvm-cpu.

Grouped dequantization matches the PT2E reference, including bf16
scales. The per-channel-group reference adds the zero point before
rounding, so exact ties round differently for odd zero points, as they
do in Torch-to-Linalg.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-channel-group quantization to LinalgExt

Convert the typed PT2E quantize_per_channel_group and
dequantize_per_channel_group ops to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and
dequantize_affine before Torch-to-Linalg expands them, so later QDQ
optimizations keep the group structure instead of floordiv-indexed
arithmetic. LinalgExt indexes parameters with projected permutations, so
the ops work on the input with its last dimension split into groups and
their result is collapsed back; the type of that view is derived from
the group size in one place. A group size beyond the row with one scale
per row is read as a single group spanning the row, as PT2E does.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express remain for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering:
groups that do not evenly split a static last dimension of a rank-2
input, flattened group parameters, bool zero points, which LinalgExt
would sign-extend to -1, non-float real values, and f16 or bf16 scales
on quantize, which would round f32 real values and currently fail to
link on llvm-cpu.

Grouped dequantization matches the PT2E reference, including bf16
scales. The per-channel-group reference adds the zero point before
rounding, so exact ties round differently for odd zero points, as they
do in Torch-to-Linalg.

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-channel-group quantization to LinalgExt

Convert the typed PT2E quantize_per_channel_group and
dequantize_per_channel_group ops to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and
dequantize_affine before Torch-to-Linalg expands them, so later QDQ
optimizations keep the group structure instead of floordiv-indexed
arithmetic. LinalgExt indexes parameters with projected permutations, so
the ops work on the input with its last dimension split into groups and
their result is collapsed back; the type of that view is derived from
the group size in one place. A group size beyond the row with one scale
per row is read as a single group spanning the row, as PT2E does.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express remain for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering:
groups that do not evenly split a static last dimension of a rank-2
input, flattened group parameters, bool zero points, which LinalgExt
would sign-extend to -1, non-float real values, and f16 or bf16 scales
on quantize, which would round f32 real values and currently fail to
link on llvm-cpu.

Grouped dequantization matches the PT2E reference, including bf16
scales. The per-channel-group reference adds the zero point before
rounding, so exact ties round differently for odd zero points, as they
do in Torch-to-Linalg.

commit_message:
[CI] Run Vulkan HAL CTS under rocjitsu (#25001)

Extend the Vulkan simulator helper to select HAL CTS alongside the
existing e2e tests on gfx1100 and gfx1201. Reuse the same CI job, build,
and pinned TheRock SDK.

Give the raw SPIR-V CTS executable a five-minute timeout. Its concurrent
replay case submits two dispatches of 8M workgroups and takes just over
a minute on simulated gfx1100, exceeding the previous 60-second limit.
Regenerate the CMake test definition from Bazel.

The assertions-enabled local run passes all 192 selected test
executables on each GPU, including 43 HAL CTS executables, with existing
per-case capability skips retained. Shell, actionlint, and pre-commit
checks pass.

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5

Updates LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5. The GPU min/maxnumf carry
patch is dropped now that it landed upstream (llvm/llvm-project@2e686411fa67).

Compatibility changes:

- Migrate AMDGPU target handling from the deprecated `amdgpu::Chipset`
  (ISA version numbers) to `ROCDL::TargetInfo` (target feature queries),
  following llvm/llvm-project@155462f440ff. The upstream AMDGPU/ROCDL
  lowering entry points now take a `ROCDL::TargetInfo`, and the remaining
  `Chipset` uses in IREE are migrated too since the deprecation warnings
  fail the Bazel `-Werror` build. Behavior is preserved except where
  upstream corrected it:
  - Barriers on targets without hardware barrier back-off (e.g. gfx90c)
    use the inline-asm `s_barrier` form, matching upstream.
  - OCP fp8 conversions are also recognized on gfx11.7.
  - The wave64 flag for the HIP platform globals is derived from the
    target, so wave32-only targets such as gfx1250 are handled correctly.
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced by
  llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

Updates LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5. The GPU min/maxnumf carry
patch is dropped now that it landed upstream (llvm/llvm-project@2e686411fa67).

Compatibility changes:

- Migrate AMDGPU target handling from the deprecated `amdgpu::Chipset`
  (ISA version numbers) to `ROCDL::TargetInfo` (target feature queries),
  following llvm/llvm-project@155462f440ff. The upstream AMDGPU/ROCDL
  lowering entry points now take a `ROCDL::TargetInfo`, and the remaining
  `Chipset` uses in IREE are migrated too since the deprecation warnings
  fail the Bazel `-Werror` build. Behavior is preserved except where
  upstream corrected it:
  - Barriers on targets without hardware barrier back-off (e.g. gfx90c)
    use the inline-asm `s_barrier` form, matching upstream.
  - OCP fp8 conversions are also recognized on gfx11.7.
  - The wave64 flag for the HIP platform globals is derived from the
    target, so wave32-only targets such as gfx1250 are handled correctly.
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced by
  llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: runtime :: ubuntu-24.04-arm

Updates LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5. The GPU min/maxnumf carry
patch is dropped now that it landed upstream (llvm/llvm-project@2e686411fa67).

Compatibility changes:

- Migrate AMDGPU target handling from the deprecated `amdgpu::Chipset`
  (ISA version numbers) to `ROCDL::TargetInfo` (target feature queries),
  following llvm/llvm-project@155462f440ff. The upstream AMDGPU/ROCDL
  lowering entry points now take a `ROCDL::TargetInfo`, and the remaining
  `Chipset` uses in IREE are migrated too since the deprecation warnings
  fail the Bazel `-Werror` build. Behavior is preserved except where
  upstream corrected it:
  - Barriers on targets without hardware barrier back-off (e.g. gfx90c)
    use the inline-asm `s_barrier` form, matching upstream.
  - OCP fp8 conversions are also recognized on gfx11.7.
  - The wave64 flag for the HIP platform globals is derived from the
    target, so wave32-only targets such as gfx1250 are handled correctly.
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced by
  llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: Test Sharktank / sharktank_tests :: cpu_task

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-channel-group quantization to LinalgExt

Convert the typed PT2E quantize_per_channel_group and
dequantize_per_channel_group ops to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and
dequantize_affine before Torch-to-Linalg expands them, so later QDQ
optimizations keep the group structure instead of floordiv-indexed
arithmetic. LinalgExt indexes parameters with projected permutations, so
the ops work on the input with its last dimension split into groups and
their result is collapsed back; the type of that view is derived from
the group size in one place. A group size beyond the row with one scale
per row is read as a single group spanning the row, as PT2E does.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express remain for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering:
groups that do not evenly split a static last dimension of a rank-2
input, flattened group parameters, bool zero points, which LinalgExt
would sign-extend to -1, non-float real values, and f16 or bf16 scales
on quantize, which would round f32 real values and currently fail to
link on llvm-cpu.

Grouped dequantization matches the PT2E reference, including bf16
scales. The per-channel-group reference adds the zero point before
rounding, so exact ties round differently for odd zero points, as they
do in Torch-to-Linalg.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-channel-group quantization to LinalgExt

Convert the typed PT2E quantize_per_channel_group and
dequantize_per_channel_group ops to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and
dequantize_affine before Torch-to-Linalg expands them, so later QDQ
optimizations keep the group structure instead of floordiv-indexed
arithmetic. LinalgExt indexes parameters with projected permutations, so
the ops work on the input with its last dimension split into groups and
their result is collapsed back; the type of that view is derived from
the group size in one place. A group size beyond the row with one scale
per row is read as a single group spanning the row, as PT2E does.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express remain for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering:
groups that do not evenly split a static last dimension of a rank-2
input, flattened group parameters, bool zero points, which LinalgExt
would sign-extend to -1, non-float real values, and f16 or bf16 scales
on quantize, which would round f32 real values and currently fail to
link on llvm-cpu.

Grouped dequantization matches the PT2E reference, including bf16
scales. The per-channel-group reference adds the zero point before
rounding, so exact ties round differently for odd zero points, as they
do in Torch-to-Linalg.

commit_message:
Migrate IREE dialects to strict properties (#24983)

LLVM deprecated the legacy assembly treatment of attributes in
llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4. IREE temporarily opted eight dialects
out during the LLVM integrate; this change removes those opt-outs and
migrates them to strict properties.

Update Codegen, VectorExt, Flow, HAL, LinalgExt, Stream, Util, and VM
assembly formats, fixtures, examples, and generators. Add roundtrip
coverage distinguishing properties from discardable attributes.

commit_message:
[Vulkan] Keep a rejected queue_dealloca from clearing a pending one

queue_dealloca rolled back the transient's dealloca_queued flag on every
error, including when begin_dealloca had rejected the call because another
dealloca was already queued. The rejected call cleared the pending
dealloca's flag, so a third call was accepted and the buffer was queued for
release twice. A call with unsupported flags cleared it the same way.

Return before begin_dealloca on argument errors and when begin_dealloca
rejects the call, as the AMDGPU host queue does, so only the call that set
the flag rolls it back.

The tests live in the Vulkan CTS rather than hal/cts/queue because the HAL
contract does not define a second dealloca of the same buffer and the local
drivers accept it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Vulkan] Keep a rejected queue_dealloca from clearing a pending one

queue_dealloca rolled back the transient's dealloca_queued flag on every
error, including when begin_dealloca had rejected the call because another
dealloca was already queued. The rejected call cleared the pending
dealloca's flag, so a third call was accepted and the buffer was queued for
release twice. A call with unsupported flags cleared it the same way.

Return before begin_dealloca on argument errors and when begin_dealloca
rejects the call, as the AMDGPU host queue does, so only the call that set
the flag rolls it back.

The tests live in the Vulkan CTS rather than hal/cts/queue because the HAL
contract does not define a second dealloca of the same buffer and the local
drivers accept it.

error, including when begin_dealloca had rejected the call because another
dealloca was already queued. The rejected call cleared the pending
dealloca's flag, so a third call was accepted and the buffer was queued for
release twice. A call with unsupported flags cleared it the same way.

Return before begin_dealloca on argument errors and when begin_dealloca
rejects the call, as the AMDGPU host queue does, so only the call that set
the flag rolls it back.

The tests live in the Vulkan CTS rather than hal/cts/queue because the HAL
contract does not define a second dealloca of the same buffer and the local
drivers accept it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions (#24966)

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves, and
add the function pass
`iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-data-tiling-encodings` for propagation
outside dispatches. Hoisting keeps its existing behavior. The new pass
stops at existing dispatches and block boundaries, and constant CSE
stays disabled because Flow regions do not materialize constants
themselves.

- `iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings` runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps `set_encoding` with `tensor.cast`
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
They stay separate until bubbling through generic ops goes through the
encoding propagation interfaces (TODO(#20179)).
- Bubbling now stops at `set_encoding` ops whose encoding is not an
`EncodingAttr`, such as `#iree_encoding.padding`, instead of crashing.
`iree-dispatch-creation-hoist-encoding-ops` could already hit this
within dispatches; both passes have a regression test.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental
early data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

Assisted by AI.
name: Analyze (python)

commit_message:
Update release process docs and make pypi_deploy.sh dry-run by default

* pypi_deploy.sh: dry run by default (`twine check`), `--publish` to upload.
  `--wheel-dir` publishes the wheels of a previous dry run without
  downloading them again. Missing packages need confirmation, and each
  package is uploaded separately so one failure does not stop the others.
* Add a release tracker template and document filing it with `gh`.
* release-management.md: document the missing tracker steps (breaking
  changes, release notes, iree-turbine, version bump), the `gh` commands
  for creating the GitHub release, and where to find the VMFB bytecode and
  HAL module versions.
* RELEASING.md: fix the iree-turbine release docs link.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

* pypi_deploy.sh: dry run by default (`twine check`), `--publish` to upload.
  `--wheel-dir` publishes the wheels of a previous dry run without
  downloading them again. Missing packages need confirmation, and each
  package is uploaded separately so one failure does not stop the others.
* Add a release tracker template and document filing it with `gh`.
* release-management.md: document the missing tracker steps (breaking
  changes, release notes, iree-turbine, version bump), the `gh` commands
  for creating the GitHub release, and where to find the VMFB bytecode and
  HAL module versions.
* RELEASING.md: fix the iree-turbine release docs link.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Torch] Preserve PT2E quantization as LinalgExt ops (#24918)

Converts the typed PT2E `quantized_decomposed` per-tensor and
per-channel quantize/dequantize ops to `iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine`
/ `dequantize_affine` during Torch input conversion, before
Torch-to-Linalg expands them into scalar arithmetic.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express (fp8 storage, non-constant bounds or axis,
an axis outside the input rank, unknown dtypes) stay on the existing
Torch-to-Linalg path. Well-formedness of the Torch ops is left to their
verifiers.

Per-tensor scales are applied in f32 for both directions, matching
Inductor, which computes in f32 and rounds once to the result dtype.

Part of #24862.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commit_message:
[CI] Run Vulkan HAL CTS under rocjitsu

Extend the Vulkan simulator helper to select HAL CTS alongside the
existing e2e tests on gfx1100 and gfx1201. Reuse the same CI job, build,
and pinned TheRock SDK.

Give the raw SPIR-V CTS executable a five-minute timeout. Its concurrent
replay case submits two dispatches of 8M workgroups and takes just over
a minute on simulated gfx1100, exceeding the previous 60-second limit.
Regenerate the CMake test definition from Bazel.

The assertions-enabled local run passes all 192 selected test executables
on each GPU, including 43 HAL CTS executables, with existing per-case
capability skips retained. Shell, actionlint, and pre-commit checks pass.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions (#24966)

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves, and
add the function pass
`iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-data-tiling-encodings` for propagation
outside dispatches. Hoisting keeps its existing behavior. The new pass
stops at existing dispatches and block boundaries, and constant CSE
stays disabled because Flow regions do not materialize constants
themselves.

- `iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings` runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps `set_encoding` with `tensor.cast`
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
They stay separate until bubbling through generic ops goes through the
encoding propagation interfaces (TODO(#20179)).
- Bubbling now stops at `set_encoding` ops whose encoding is not an
`EncodingAttr`, such as `#iree_encoding.padding`, instead of crashing.
`iree-dispatch-creation-hoist-encoding-ops` could already hit this
within dispatches; both passes have a regression test.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental
early data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

Assisted by AI.

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5

Updates LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5. The GPU min/maxnumf carry
patch is dropped now that it landed upstream (llvm/llvm-project@2e686411fa67).

Compatibility changes:

- Migrate AMDGPU target handling from the deprecated `amdgpu::Chipset`
  (ISA version numbers) to `ROCDL::TargetInfo` (target feature queries),
  following llvm/llvm-project@155462f440ff. The upstream AMDGPU/ROCDL
  lowering entry points now take a `ROCDL::TargetInfo`, and the remaining
  `Chipset` uses in IREE are migrated too since the deprecation warnings
  fail the Bazel `-Werror` build. Behavior is preserved except where
  upstream corrected it:
  - Barrier lowering is gated on the barrier back-off feature instead of
    the ISA version; no change for any IREE-supported target.
  - OCP fp8 conversions are also recognized on gfx11.7.
  - The wave64 flag for the HIP platform globals is derived from the
    target, so wave32-only targets such as gfx1250 are handled correctly.
- The wave size is now part of the target description, and targets that
  support both wave32 and wave64 resolve to wave32 by default. ConvertToROCDL
  therefore resolves the variant's subgroup size (which IREE already requires
  to be uniform per variant) and threads it through, so a wave64 dispatch on
  RDNA is described as wave64. Requesting a wave size the target cannot run
  (e.g. wave64 on gfx1250) is now rejected with a diagnostic.
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced by
  llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5

Updates LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5. The GPU min/maxnumf carry
patch is dropped now that it landed upstream (llvm/llvm-project@2e686411fa67).

Compatibility changes:

- Migrate AMDGPU target handling from the deprecated `amdgpu::Chipset`
  (ISA version numbers) to `ROCDL::TargetInfo` (target feature queries),
  following llvm/llvm-project@155462f440ff. The upstream AMDGPU/ROCDL
  lowering entry points now take a `ROCDL::TargetInfo`, and the remaining
  `Chipset` uses in IREE are migrated too since the deprecation warnings
  fail the Bazel `-Werror` build. Behavior is preserved except where
  upstream corrected it:
  - Barrier lowering is gated on the barrier back-off feature instead of
    the ISA version; no change for any IREE-supported target.
  - OCP fp8 conversions are also recognized on gfx11.7.
  - The wave64 flag for the HIP platform globals is derived from the
    target, so wave32-only targets such as gfx1250 are handled correctly.
- The wave size is now part of the target description, and targets that
  support both wave32 and wave64 resolve to wave32 by default. ConvertToROCDL
  therefore resolves the variant's subgroup size (which IREE already requires
  to be uniform per variant) and threads it through, so a wave64 dispatch on
  RDNA is described as wave64. Requesting a wave size the target cannot run
  (e.g. wave64 on gfx1250) is now rejected with a diagnostic.
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced by
  llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302.

  support both wave32 and wave64 resolve to wave32 by default. ConvertToROCDL
  therefore resolves the variant's subgroup size (which IREE already requires

  RDNA is described as wave64. Requesting a wave size the target cannot run

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Keep strided input maps when the producer can fuse (#24950)

Factoring `dim * cst` strides out of a contraction-like generic inserts
a strided `tensor.extract_slice` between the contraction and its input.
When the input has an elementwise producer (a dequantize feeding a 1x1
stride-2 convolution, say), the slice blocks both fusion paths:
elementwise fusion requires the producer to directly define the
consumer's operand, and tile-based producer fusion only supports
unit-stride slices. Codegen falls back to materializing the producer as
a whole-tensor stack allocation in every workgroup: a 3.2 MB alloca for
a 1x256x56x56xf32 dequantize, well over the 32 KB stack limit, and the
compile fails.

Skip the factoring only when the strided input's producer can fuse
elementwise into the contraction and into every other user of its
result, so the fusion actually eliminates the producer. Codegen then
merges the producer into the contraction, which reads the input directly
through the strided map with no intermediate tensor. Producers that are
materialized anyway (e.g. a result also returned from the function) keep
the factored projected-permutation input map.

Strided contractions with a fusable producer now lower through the
generic path instead of contraction selection such as AMDGPU MFMA, the
original motivation for the factoring, in exchange for eliminating the
intermediate tensor. Strided contractions on dispatch-boundary inputs
keep the factored form.

Fixes #24752

commit_message:
[Bindings][Compiler] Add Bazel support for Python bindings (#24980)

IREE's compiler Python support is available through CMake, but its
generated dialect bindings, native extensions and compiler tool wrappers
are not exposed as Bazel targets. Downstream projects using Bazel
therefore need to maintain their own build definitions to package Python
bindings that match the compiler they build.

Providing these targets upstream lets consumers build Python compiler
packages against their chosen IREE revision and keeps the binding
definitions alongside the sources they describe. The bindings use
`IREECompiler`'s shared C API so Python code can inspect and construct
IR, then invoke the compiler using the same MLIR implementation.
Consumers retain control of package and wheel assembly.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions (#24966)

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves, and
add the function pass
`iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-data-tiling-encodings` for propagation
outside dispatches. Hoisting keeps its existing behavior. The new pass
stops at existing dispatches and block boundaries, and constant CSE
stays disabled because Flow regions do not materialize constants
themselves.

- `iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings` runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps `set_encoding` with `tensor.cast`
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
They stay separate until bubbling through generic ops goes through the
encoding propagation interfaces (TODO(#20179)).
- Bubbling now stops at `set_encoding` ops whose encoding is not an
`EncodingAttr`, such as `#iree_encoding.padding`, instead of crashing.
`iree-dispatch-creation-hoist-encoding-ops` could already hit this
within dispatches; both passes have a regression test.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental
early data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

commit_message:
[Torch] Preserve PT2E quantization as LinalgExt ops (#24918)

Converts the typed PT2E `quantized_decomposed` per-tensor and
per-channel quantize/dequantize ops to `iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine`
/ `dequantize_affine` during Torch input conversion, before
Torch-to-Linalg expands them into scalar arithmetic.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express (fp8 storage, non-constant bounds or axis,
an axis outside the input rank, unknown dtypes) stay on the existing
Torch-to-Linalg path. Well-formedness of the Torch ops is left to their
verifiers.

Per-tensor scales are applied in f32 for both directions, matching
Inductor, which computes in f32 and rounds once to the result dtype.

Part of #24862.

  `--wheel-dir` publishes the wheels of a previous dry run without
  downloading them again. Missing packages need confirmation, and each
  package is uploaded separately so one failure does not stop the others.
* Add a release tracker template and document filing it with `gh`.
* release-management.md: document the missing tracker steps (breaking
  changes, release notes, iree-turbine, version bump), the `gh` commands
  for creating the GitHub release, and where to find the VMFB bytecode and
  HAL module versions.
* RELEASING.md: fix the iree-turbine release docs link.

commit_message:
[Vulkan] Keep a rejected queue_dealloca from clearing a pending one

queue_dealloca rolled back the transient's dealloca_queued flag on every
error, including when begin_dealloca had rejected the call because another
dealloca was already queued. The rejected call cleared the pending
dealloca's flag, so a third call was accepted and the buffer was queued for
release twice. A call with unsupported flags cleared it the same way.

Return before begin_dealloca on argument errors and when begin_dealloca
rejects the call, as the AMDGPU host queue does, so only the call that set
the flag rolls it back.

The tests live in the Vulkan CTS rather than hal/cts/queue because the HAL
contract does not define a second dealloca of the same buffer and the local
drivers accept it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
Migrate IREE dialects to strict properties (#24983)

LLVM deprecated the legacy assembly treatment of attributes in
llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4. IREE temporarily opted eight dialects
out during the LLVM integrate; this change removes those opt-outs and
migrates them to strict properties.

Update Codegen, VectorExt, Flow, HAL, LinalgExt, Stream, Util, and VM
assembly formats, fixtures, examples, and generators. Add roundtrip
coverage distinguishing properties from discardable attributes.

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5

Updates LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5. The GPU min/maxnumf carry
patch is dropped now that it landed upstream (llvm/llvm-project@2e686411fa67).

Compatibility changes:

- Migrate AMDGPU target handling from the deprecated `amdgpu::Chipset`
  (ISA version numbers) to `ROCDL::TargetInfo` (target feature queries),
  following llvm/llvm-project@155462f440ff. The upstream AMDGPU/ROCDL
  lowering entry points now take a `ROCDL::TargetInfo`, and the remaining
  `Chipset` uses in IREE are migrated too since the deprecation warnings
  fail the Bazel `-Werror` build. Behavior is preserved except where

Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5

Updates LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5. The GPU min/maxnumf carry
patch is dropped now that it landed upstream (llvm/llvm-project@2e686411fa67).

Compatibility changes:

- Migrate AMDGPU target handling from the deprecated `amdgpu::Chipset`
  (ISA version numbers) to `ROCDL::TargetInfo` (target feature queries),
  following llvm/llvm-project@155462f440ff. The upstream AMDGPU/ROCDL
  lowering entry points now take a `ROCDL::TargetInfo`, and the remaining
  `Chipset` uses in IREE are migrated too since the deprecation warnings
  fail the Bazel `-Werror` build. Behavior is preserved except where
  upstream corrected it:
  - Barriers on targets without hardware barrier back-off (e.g. gfx90c)
    use the inline-asm `s_barrier` form, matching upstream.
  - OCP fp8 conversions are also recognized on gfx11.7.
  - The wave64 flag for the HIP platform globals is derived from the
    target, so wave32-only targets such as gfx1250 are handled correctly.
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced by
  llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302.

commit_message:
[CI] Run Vulkan HAL CTS under rocjitsu (#25001)

Extend the Vulkan simulator helper to select HAL CTS alongside the
existing e2e tests on gfx1100 and gfx1201. Reuse the same CI job, build,
and pinned TheRock SDK.

Give the raw SPIR-V CTS executable a five-minute timeout. Its concurrent
replay case submits two dispatches of 8M workgroups and takes just over
a minute on simulated gfx1100, exceeding the previous 60-second limit.
Regenerate the CMake test definition from Bazel.

The assertions-enabled local run passes all 192 selected test
executables on each GPU, including 43 HAL CTS executables, with existing
per-case capability skips retained. Shell, actionlint, and pre-commit
checks pass.

Assisted-by: codex

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-channel-group quantization to LinalgExt

Convert the typed PT2E quantize_per_channel_group and
dequantize_per_channel_group ops to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and
dequantize_affine before Torch-to-Linalg expands them, so later QDQ
optimizations keep the group structure instead of floordiv-indexed
arithmetic. LinalgExt indexes parameters with projected permutations, so
the ops work on the input with its last dimension split into groups and
their result is collapsed back; the type of that view is derived from
the group size in one place. A group size beyond the row with one scale
per row is read as a single group spanning the row, as PT2E does.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express remain for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering:
groups that do not evenly split a static last dimension of a rank-2
input, flattened group parameters, bool zero points, which LinalgExt
would sign-extend to -1, non-float real values, and f16 or bf16 scales
on quantize, which would round f32 real values and currently fail to
link on llvm-cpu.

Grouped dequantization matches the PT2E reference, including bf16
scales. The per-channel-group reference adds the zero point before
rounding, so exact ties round differently for odd zero points, as they
do in Torch-to-Linalg.

commit_message:
[CI] Run Vulkan HAL CTS under rocjitsu (#25001)

Extend the Vulkan simulator helper to select HAL CTS alongside the
existing e2e tests on gfx1100 and gfx1201. Reuse the same CI job, build,
and pinned TheRock SDK.

Give the raw SPIR-V CTS executable a five-minute timeout. Its concurrent
replay case submits two dispatches of 8M workgroups and takes just over
a minute on simulated gfx1100, exceeding the previous 60-second limit.
Regenerate the CMake test definition from Bazel.

The assertions-enabled local run passes all 192 selected test
executables on each GPU, including 43 HAL CTS executables, with existing
per-case capability skips retained. Shell, actionlint, and pre-commit
checks pass.

Assisted-by: codex
